articles.title: Teofimo Lopez Beats Rolly Romero for 3rd Title, Final Judges' Scorecards, Prize Money & Highlights
articles.summary: Teofimo Lopez became a champion across three different divisions Saturday night thanks to his victory over Rolly Romero.
articles.body:
Teofimo Lopez became a champion across three different divisions Saturday night thanks to his victory over Rolly Romero.

Lopez claimed a majority decision. One judge scored it 114-114, but the two others in Lopez's favor (115-113 and 116-112).

The 29-year-old is now the WBA welterweight champion, having previously earned belts in the light welterweight and lightweight divisions.

Lopez owned a sizable edge in the punching stats. According to CompuBox , he landed 124 total blows to 73 for Romero, including 62 power punches.

Despite what the raw numbers showed, Romero thought he was the better fighter on the night.

"I got hit with two punches the whole fight that barely grazed me," he said, per ESPN's Brett Okamoto . "I was never in any trouble. When I heard 114-114, I knew it was a robbery."

In the fifth round, Romero connected flush with a right hook and then went in with a flurry of blows. Lopez briefly fell to his knees, but the referee didn't call it a knockdown.

That round was Romero's best. After getting tagged, Lopez was sharper and defended much better. If anything, the judges' scores didn't give him enough credit on balance.

This was the kind of performance Lopez needed after losing a unanimous decision to Shakur Stevenson in January. Now, he can look ahead to another big-money fight.

Lopez suggested he could go against the winner of Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn, who step between the ropes Sept. 12 in Las Vegas, or IBF welterweight champion Liam Paro. He brought up Devin Haney as well but clarified he'd "rather wait" on that matchup.

articles.title: AEW's Athena Reveals Asthma Attack During ROH Match as New Video Surfaces
articles.summary: All Elite Wrestling star and Ring of Honor women's world champion Athena divulged Saturday that she suffered an asthma attack in the middle of her main event match against Hazuki at Death Before Dishonor on Friday.
articles.body:
All Elite Wrestling star and Ring of Honor women's world champion Athena divulged Saturday that she suffered an asthma attack in the middle of her main event match against Hazuki at Death Before Dishonor on Friday.

In response to a viral video of Billie Starkz humorously yelling at a fan who called for Athena to get up while she was laying down outside the ring, Athena made a post on X about the asthma attack:

As part of her post, Athena thanked the ROH staff for the "quick response" to her episode.

Athena, who previously wrestled under the name Ember Moon in WWE, is the active and longest-reigning ROH women's world champion of all time, having held the title for well over 1,300 days.

Despite the asthma attack, she had yet another successful title defense against Hazuki on Friday and continued her run as one of the most dominant champions in all of pro wrestling.

articles.title: Watch UFC Legends Henry Cejudo and Merab Dvalishvili's Full Highlights from 'Stunning' RAF 12 Match
articles.summary: Longtime UFC stars Henry Cejudo and Merab Dvalishvili once again brought their rivalry to the wrestling mat in the main event of RAF 12 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Longtime UFC stars Henry Cejudo and Merab Dvalishvili once again brought their rivalry to the wrestling mat in the main event of RAF 12 on Saturday night.

Cejudo, who lost to Dvalishvili at UFC 298 in 2024 in a dominant unanimous decision and again at RAF Georgia last month, got his revenge with a "stunning" 36-second pinfall victory:

In their first freestyle wrestling meeting last month, Cejudo was leading 8-0 before Dvalishvili stormed back for an 11-8 victory. This time around, Cejudo left no doubt, as the Olympic gold medalist scored a quick takedown before swiftly pinning his rival's shoulders to the mat.

"Merab is a machine," Cejudo said after his win, per Damon Martin of MMA Fighting. "I've been fighting for 13 years on my feet and I took the 'L' from him. I knew that he wasn't necessarily scrambling … obviously I got the pin."

After the victory, Cejudo set his sights on another longtime UFC veteran.

"Cody Garbrandt, you're next b---h," he said.

Dvalishvili, who is gearing up for a trilogy fight against UFC bantamweight champion Petr Yan at UFC 333 on Oct. 24, also expressed interest in returning to RAF for a rubber match against Cejudo.

"Absoutely. I love challenges," Dvalishvili said. "Henry Cejudo called me out and I said yes. He's an Olympic champion for a reason. He beat me today. Let's go for a trilogy in wrestling."

articles.title: UFC Legend Tyron Woodley Snaps 8-Year Losing Streak After Win at RAF 12 Before Khamzat Chimaev Fight
articles.summary: UFC legend Tyron Woodley had his hand raised in victory for the first time in eight years at RAF 12 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
UFC legend Tyron Woodley had his hand raised in victory for the first time in eight years at RAF 12 on Saturday night.

Woodley, who hadn't won in MMA or boxing since a 2018 UFC welterweight title defense against Darren Till, recorded a 14-8 comeback victory over UFC veteran Joaquin Buckley in his RAF debut.

Things appeared dire for Woodley early on, as he fell behind 8-0 against Buckley. However, he chipped away at the lead with multiple reversals before landing a huge takedown to seal the win.

"I knew better [than to underestimate Buckley]," Woodley said after the match, per Damon Martin of MMA Fighting. "It's bragging rights. When I got down, I didn't lose my composure."

Woodley already has his next match lined up, as he will face former UFC middleweight champion Khamzat Chimaev in the main event of RAF Moscow on Sept. 5. Saturday's win will surely give him some confidence as he goes up against an aggressive wrestler like Chimaev next month.

articles.title: Cris Cyborg Calls Out Claressa Shields, Full Judges' Scorecards and Highlights from Win vs. Vieira
articles.summary: While MMA legend Cris Cyborg was expected to retire after her PFL featherweight title defense against Ketlen Vieira on Saturday night, she still has her eyes set on a future big-name opponent.
articles.body:
While MMA legend Cris Cyborg was expected to retire after her PFL featherweight title defense against Ketlen Vieira on Saturday night, she still has her eyes set on a future big-name opponent.

Cyborg defeated Vieira by unanimous decision with scores of 49-46, 48-47, 49-46 in the main event of PFL Tampa to earn her 30th career MMA win.

After the victory, Cyborg didn't commit to hanging up her gloves, and she called out boxing star Claressa Shields for a future fight.

"I'm ready for anybody," Cyborg said, per Drake Riggs of Uncrowned. "I'm not a free agent. I'm going back to rest. Eight years undefeated. I'm ready for anybody. Any time, any weight. [Boxing champion] Claressa Shields, the girl is scared to fight me. You're scared. [Vieira] has more heart than you. … Eat less. [Let's fight at] 160 [pounds]. Let's go."

Shields, who won the WBA and WBC female middleweight titles earlier this month, wasn't the only potential adversary on Cyborg's mind. Former two-time PFL champion and reigning UFC bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison was in attendance to watch her teammates compete on the fight card, and Cyborg also targeted her for a potential matchup.

"Kayla Harrison is here. Come here!" Cyborg said. "Hey, Kayla. You've been running for so long. You went running from PFL from me, now you come to watch my fight. I'm ready for you. I hope you heal your neck and go challenge Amanda Nunes, and I'm here."

Cyborg is one of the greatest women's fighters in combat sports history, so it wouldn't be a surprise if she looks to extend her iconic career with another marquee showdown.

articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: Claressa Shields open to facing  Mikaela Mayer if she does not secure Lauren Price fight
articles.summary: Claressa Shields has declared 'I beat everybody' and could be open to facing Mikaela Mayer if she does not fight Lauren Price next; Mayer takes on Chantelle Cameron on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, in a super-welterweight world title unification clash
articles.body:
The multi-weight world champion has been in talks for a middleweight fight against Britain's Lauren Price , who is a fellow Olympic gold medallist.

But if Price is not her next opponent, then Shields could switch her attention to Mayer, who faces Chantelle Cameron in a super-welterweight world title unification fight on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

"Anything is possible," Shields told Sky Sports . "I came down [in weight] specifically to fight against Kaye Scott and then hopefully have a big showdown with Olympic champions, me and Lauren Price.

"If the fight with Lauren Price can't happen, I would love to get in the ring with Mikaela Mayer.

"I know that she came from a smaller weight class and now she's at 154lbs, but my skills are still better than hers.

"I'm still faster than her. We have the same experience but I have better experience. I've been to the Olympic gold medal match twice, she hasn't.

"I beat everybody. It doesn't matter the name that you put. Claressa versus whoever, I beat them."

Mayer is fully focused on defeating Cameron, but admits that fights against Shields and Price are still on her hitlist.

"Obviously, I would love to get the fight with Lauren Price," Mayer told Sky Sports .

"Claressa Shields and I have spoken about potentially fighting at 160lbs which I would love to do.

"In a perfect world, I would get all three of those fights back-to-back and sail away into the sunset."

Shields became a middleweight world champion for a third time after ruthlessly stopping Kaye Scott this month, racking up her 19th straight victory in the professional ranks with no defeats.

Floyd Mayweather, who stepped away from his pro career after 50 wins, was watching from ringside and Shields believes she can emulate him by preserving her perfect record.

"I had the biggest names there. I sold the arena out. It was insane," said Shields.

"I put on a great performance. I've been building my career to this point, so I'm happy.

"I believe that I can retire undefeated, that's my goal. I don't know if I'll ever get 50 fights, but 30 is good for me."

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron: Super-welterweight unification fight in Birmingham live on Sky Sports

articles.body:
America's Mayer, the reigning WBA and WBC champion, faces Britain's Cameron, the WBO champion, over 12 rounds, with the winner capturing three of the division's four belts and moving a step closer to a shot at undisputed status.

The fight headlines MVPW-06 and tops a card that pits a UK fighter against a US opponent in almost every bout.

Mayer and Cameron will collide on Saturday August 29, live on Sky Sports.

Live coverage of the action-packed bill in Birmingham starts at 7pm on Sky Sports.

Birmingham's BP Pulse LIVE Arena is the host venue of MVPW-06 as a landmark night for women's boxing unfolds in Britain's 'Second City'.

The ring walks for Mayer vs Cameron are expected between 9.30pm and 10pm on Saturday night.

Who else is on the Mayer vs Cameron bill?

In the chief support bout, unified WBC and WBO lightweight world champion Caroline Dubois takes on former US Olympian Amelia Moore.

Three-weight world champion Terri Harper also features on the card, returning against Miranda Reyes at super-welterweight.

The two world title fights between Mayer and Cameron and Dubois and Moore represents the most significant women's boxing card held in Birmingham in recent history.

Yes. Alycia Baumgardner, who is bitter rival of Dubois and a former opponent of Mayer, is expected to be watching from ringside. Victory for Dubois could put her on a collision course with Baumgardner.

Promoter Jake Paul will also be in attendance for the blockbuster night of action.

You can watch a live stream of the undercard fights on the Sky Sports website and app and on Sky Sports YouTube from around 5pm on Saturday.

With the winner of three of the four belts, all eyes will be on an undisputed showdown with IBF champion Oshae Jones for the right to be crowned queen of the 154lb division.

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Date, ringwalk, UK time, undercard, venue, records & how to follow on the BBC
articles.summary: All you need to know about Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgovic and Mikaela Mayer v Chantelle Cameron before the fights on Saturday.
articles.body:
On Saturday's boxing double-header, Moses Itauma bids to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion against Filip Hrgovic, while Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron meet in a major world title unification clash.

Briton Itauma, 21, is one of boxing's brightest young talents, with 14 wins and 12 knockouts. Hrgovic, 34, brings a 20-1 record and years of top-level experience, with his only defeat coming against Daniel Dubois.

Can Itauma take down Hrgovic at London's O2 Arena and win the vacant IBF title? Or will the Croatian's experience and power end the hype?

Meanwhile, Mayer and Briton Cameron collide in a three-belt light-middleweight unification fight at BP Pulse Arena in Birmingham. American Mayer holds the WBA and WBC titles, while Cameron owns the WBO belt.

The bout pits two top elite fighters against each other, with both aiming to move one step closer to becoming undisputed.

Here is all you need to know about Itauma v Hrgovic and Mayer v Cameron.

Itauma v Hrgovic upgraded to IBF world-title bout

From influencers to queens of women's boxing - five years of MVP

Hrgovic taunts starting to wind me up - Itauma

How to follow Itauma v Hrgovic & Mayer v Cameron on the BBC

Radio commentary of Itauma v Hrgovic from London will begin at 21:00 BST on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds, and the BBC Sport website and app, before switching to 5 Live from 22:00 on Saturday, 29 August.

Coverage will be presented by Ugo Monye, with Ronald McIntosh as lead commentator, alongside former super-middleweight world champion Richie Woodhall and boxing expert Steve Bunce.

Live text commentary of both cards will begin at 19:30 on the BBC Sport website and app.

The Birmingham event also features a strong female undercard, with unified lightweight champion Caroline Dubois defending her WBC and WBO titles against Amelia Moore, while former three-weight world champion Terri Harper is also in action.

We will bring you round-by-round updates of Dubois v Moore and Mayer v Cameron.

You can also follow the action through fight week on BBC Sport via the 5 Live Boxing podcast.

Itauma and Hrgovic are not expected to make their walk to the ring before 22:00 BST.

In Birmingham, the Dubois v Moore and Mayer v Cameron ringwalk times are still to be confirmed.

All timings are estimated and are subject to change.

Itauma v Hrgovic undercard & running order

Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgovic - vacant IBF heavyweight world title

Sam Noakes v Denys Berinchyk - lightweight

Constantin Ursu v Ben Vaughan - British & Commonwealth welterweight title

Aloys Junior v Mike Perez - cruiserweight

Mayer v Cameron undercard & running order

Mikaela Mayer (c) v Chantelle Cameron (c) - WBA, WBC & WBO light-middleweight world titles

Caroline Dubois v Amelia Moore - WBC & WBO lightweight world titles

Reina Tellez v Jessica Barry - featherweight

Terri Harper v Miranda Reyes - light-welterweight

Tysie Gallagher v Ashleigh Johnson - super-bantamweight

Itauma has been earmarked for greatness since he was a teenager. He was sparring seasoned professionals while still at school.

Frank Warren took notice after seeing the schoolboy hold his own against one of his heavyweights and began sponsoring him before eventually signing him to Queensberry as a professional.

The 21-year-old has since lived up to the hype. His two biggest wins came against Dillian Whyte, who he stopped in the first round in August 2025, and Jermaine Franklin, who he knocked out in the fifth round in March.

Victory over Hrgovic would see Itauma become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion in history, behind Mike Tyson.

The IBF title became vacant after Oleksandr Usyk vacated his heavyweight belts, with the organisation initially ordering Itauma to face Cuban Frank Sanchez. Itauma had already agreed to fight Hrgovic, however, and Sanchez has accepted a step-aside deal that guarantees him a shot at the winner.

If Itauma can get through Hrgovic - an Olympic bronze medallist with a wealth of top-level experience - and then Sanchez, an all-British unification fight with either Daniel Dubois or Fabio Wardley could be on the horizon next year.

Dubois dethroned Wardley with an 11th-round stoppage in May to win the WBO title, with a rematch expected to take place in October.

Cameron was at the peak of her powers when she beat Katie Taylor by majority decision in Dublin in May 2023, handing the Irish superstar the first professional defeat of her career.

Taylor avenged that loss five months later, but Cameron's career subsequently stalled somewhat as she struggled to secure the biggest fights.

She has now reignited it under Most Valuable Promotions, co-owned by Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, becoming a two-weight world champion when she beat Michaela Kotaskova for the vacant WBO light-middleweight title in April.

Now, Cameron, 22-1 (8 KOs), has the chance to prove she remains one of the very best fighters in the world against Mayer. The American, 22-2 (5 KOs), is a three-division world champion and is fighting for the first time under MVP.

The winner will hold three of the four major belts in the division, with Oshae Jones currently holding the IBF title. Cameron knows exactly what it takes to become undisputed, having unified the light-welterweight division in 2022.

Londoner Caroline Dubois is another British star who has flourished since joining MVP, beating Harper in April to become unified champion.

Dubois is now 13-0-1 (5 KOs), while American challenger Amelia Moore enters the fight unbeaten at 4-0 (1 KO).

Dubois is a heavy favourite and is targeting IBF champion Elif Nur Turhan and WBA champion Stephanie Han as she looks to complete the lightweight undisputed puzzle, while a budding rivalry with American Alycia Baumgardner could eventually produce a blockbuster showdown.

articles.title: Predicting AEW All In 2026 Surprises From Britt Baker's Return to New Day's Debut
articles.summary: All In has been AEW's premier pay-per-view event since its inception in 2023, and the upcoming installment has the potential to be equally exceptional with what's on tap.
articles.body:
All In has been AEW's premier pay-per-view event since its inception in 2023, and the upcoming installment has the potential to be equally exceptional with what's on tap.

Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay's highly anticipated main event, Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné's AEW Women's World Championship clash and the first-time encounter over the AEW World Tag Team Championship are all guaranteed to be great from an in-ring standpoint, but there are bound to be several surprises in store as well.

All In 2024 featured Nigel McGuinness' return to the ring in his native England and Ricochet's All Elite Wrestling debut, while the returns of Bryan Danielson and Darby Allin highlighted All In 2025, so a precedent has been set for milestone moments occurring at the annual event.

From unpredictable outcomes to new champions being crowned, these are six shockers that could feasibly transpire at All In 2026.

Britt Baker Returns in Women's Casino Gauntlet

It was at All In two years ago that Britt Baker, an AEW original, had her last major match in the promotion, unsuccessfully challenging Mercedes Moné for the AEW TBS Championship.

However, the battle between two of the bigger names in women's wrestling in the last decade fell well short of fans' expectations.

Baker only made a handful of appearances on AEW TV after that before disappearing entirely from programming in November 2024. Although Tony Khan has responded to inquiries regarding her absence on media conference calls since then, her status hasn't seemed to change.

Baker was brought back up again by fans recently when Fightful Select 's Sean Ross Sapp revealed in a Q&A that she was internally discussed for the upcoming Rebel tribute edition of Dynamite on Sept. 9 in Georgia. The two were synonymous with each other in AEW's first few years.

It would make sense to reintroduce her before then in the women's Casino Gauntlet match at All In, where the winner will earn a future shot at the AEW Women's World Championship she once held.

The wrestling dentist doesn't necessarily have to win, but it would be quite the surprise to see her again amid social media rumors that she's eyeing an exit from the company due to her inactivity.

Kevin Knight is scheduled to have his biggest bout yet at All In when he defends the AEW TNT Championship against Darby Allin in a Falls Count Anywhere match.

The reigning champ is in the middle of a career year, having held the title since early April and racking up the most successful defenses for the TNT title ever. He also headlined last month's Redemption event with AEW world champion Kenny Omega and looked credible in defeat.

He's been a member of The Don Callis Family since shortly after turning heel at Double or Nothing in May, the same show where he betrayed his buddy, Darby Allin. Seeds have been planted over the last month that this new sinister side of Knight isn't the real him and that he'll soon see the light once he's away from Callis.

Perhaps it's his obsession with the gold that has made him so arrogant, and once he loses it to Allin on AEW's biggest stage, he'll realize the error of his ways.

While such a significant development for his character would be premature at this stage, it isn't completely out of the question for Sunday's pay-per-view.

Nigel McGuinness Wins the AEW Continental Championship

The ongoing Continental Challenge Cup has been a unique way of determining what the AEW Continental Championship match will be at All In, and as of this writing, only four wrestlers remain.

It will be either Jon Moxley or Claudio Castagnoli taking on Kyle O'Reilly or Nigel McGuinness for the title.

As the defending champ, Moxley should walk into the event with the belt, and seeing as how he already beat O'Reilly to retain the title in May, the finals of the tournament should be Moxley vs. McGuinness at All In.

In such a situation, Moxley would be automatically expected to emerge victorious, which would make an upset from McGuinness all the more surprising.

As noted, it was at All In two years ago that he returned to the ring for the first time since 2011 in front of his countrymen at Wembley Stadium. It would be huge for him to be the one to end Moxley's lengthy title reign on that same show two years later.

McGuinness may not be a full-time member of the active roster anymore, but it would be a fitting final chapter to his career as well as a memorable moment for those in attendance.

The New Day Win the AEW World Trios Titles with Swerve Strickland

Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods have been a hot topic of conversation among wrestling fans since receiving their release from WWE at the beginning of May.

They were always expected to have interest from AEW upon entering free agency, and now their debut may be imminent.

Swerve Strickland curiously teased challenging for the AEW World Trios Championship on a recent Dynamite. Since he doesn't currently have any established allies on the roster, it was safe for fans to assume that he could be enlisting the likes of the former New Day to go after the gold with him.

Kingston and Woods obviously belong in the tag team ranks, but there's nothing wrong with starting them out with Strickland to ensure them a spot on the show. Plus, Strickland and The New Day could turn out to be quite the formidable force.

The AEW World Trios title match for All In is not yet set in stone, but if it's some sort of multi-team affair featuring a variety of trios, look for Strickland and New Day to not only enter but also to leave as the new champions.

Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné are no strangers to each other. They've collided in both New Japan Pro-Wrestling and in AEW and have traded wins over the NJPW Strong Women's Championship and the AEW TBS Championship.

At All In, they'll meet one-on-one yet again, this time for the AEW Women's World Championship. Nightingale won the title for the first time only a month ago at Redemption, while Moné secured her shot by capturing the women's Owen Hart Cup two years in a row.

All signs point to the third time being the charm for Moné (after failing in her previous opportunities at All In 2025 and Full Gear 2025) and her taking the title that has eluded her since her arrival in the promotion, but Nightingale retaining would be the more interesting outcome.

Moné falling short would force her "crash out" to continue, and effectively turn Nightingale from a perennial chaser to a certified champion. Moné ended Nightingale's TBS title run after only one month, but history shouldn't repeat itself here.

Nightingale will again have Moné's number and pull out the win against the odds.

Sheamus, Ilja Dragunov Debut in the Men's Casino Gauntlet

The New Day may not be the only ones making their first-ever AEW appearance at All In this weekend at Wembley Stadium.

Two more familiar faces who recently left WWE on their own terms and are presumably exploring new ventures are Sheamus and Ilja Dragunov. Both men's contracts recently expired after not being featured on WWE TV for many months.

Sheamus and Dragunov were known for their intense, hard-hitting style during their time in WWE and would be perfect fits for the AEW landscape. If they are free and clear of any contractual obligation to WWE, why not have them show up during the men's Casino Gauntlet match at All In?

One of them alone would make an immediate impact, but putting them both in the same bout would be the bigger shocker of them all, similar to how Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson debuted in AEW within minutes of each other at All Out in 2021. They wouldn't be overshadowed provided they're in there for long enough and are allowed to have strong showings.

Sheamus and Dragunov being "All Elite" is inevitable, and there would be no better time or place for them to make their presence felt and potentially punch their ticket to AEW World Championship contention out of the gate.

articles.title: Blue Demon Jr., luchador: "Por mis lesiones, me metí a estudiar medicina; quiero poner salud en mis compañeros porque sé lo que es estar lastimado"
articles.standfirst: Las desgracias padecidas hicieron más fuerte al 'hijo del demonio azul'
articles.summary: Las desgracias padecidas hicieron más fuerte al 'hijo del demonio azul'
articles.body: La Lucha Libre es un deporte de alta exigencia física y atlética para ejecutar la serie de maniobras, llaves y castigos para llevarse el triunfo sobre los encordados. Sin embargo, cuando se es la víctima ante el rival en turno se expone a una serie de lesiones que lo pueden marginar del ring por un tiempo indefinido sin importar la jerarquía dentro del pancracio. Por ello mismo, el legendario luchador, Blue Demon Jr, tuvo que ponerle pausa a su carrera en diferentes ocasiones debido a las constantes heridas y cirugías a lo largo de su carrera. El 'Hijo del Demonio Azul' prepara su retiro tras más de cuatro décadas en la lucha libre y buscará dedicarse a la medicina regenerativa para ayudar a otros deportistas quienes caigan en las lesiones más comunes de esta actividad. Con alrededor de más de 60 años de edad, el flamante luchador ha impuesto respeto con su fuerza, su carácter y sus movimientos letales. Pero fuera del ring tiene una meta muy noble: sanar al prójimo. Con el pasar de los años, Blue Demon Jr ha buscado tener una preparación académica que la pudiera combinar con su actividad en la Lucha Libre. Tras una infancia de sufrimiento, cumplió su sueño de volar donde a los 18 años de edad se matriculó en el Colegio del Aire y voló una avioneta Cessna y sumó unas dos mil horas de vuelo, el cual le permitía esa libertad que tanto añoró. Una vez en los encordados, también se graduó de sistemas computacionales administrativos. Sin embargo, Blue Demon Jr también superó un cáncer en etapa 4 a los 30 años de edad, donde el doctor que lo atendió le decía que 'avanzara con su papeleo' pues era difícil que lo pudiera superar. Tras vencer esta cruel enfermedad y superar una serie de lesiones, el legendario luchador quiso agradecer a la vida y estudió medicina regenerativa. En unas semanas obtendrá el título y dedicará parte de su tiempo a curar a otros luchadores para que no tiren la toalla y mantengan sus sueños hasta el último segundo posible. El original Blue Demon comenzó un distinguido legado a finales de la década de los 50's e inmortalizado fuera de los encordados con las películas de luchadores a lado del Enmascarado de Plata, el Santo. Al pasar la batuta a su hijo adoptado, la dinastía mantuvo su popularidad hasta transcurrido el siglo XXI donde se ha convertido en un símbolo de su deporte, que en el 2008 ganó el Campeonato Mundial de la NWA (National Wrestling Alliance). Su debut en la lucha libre profesional fue en 1986, después de haber participado con la delegación de México en los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 1984 en la disciplina de Lucha. Con el paso de los años, las lesiones fueron recurrentes. La más grave en estos 40 años fue una fractura en la quinta vértebra lumbar, la cual lo dejó sin movimiento en las piernas durante ocho meses y requirió un proceso de rehabilitación muy difícil en el que incluso tuvo que arrastrarse para moverse. Pasó cerca de seis meses en silla de ruedas debido a este tipo de complicaciones severas. Estas son las lesiones que ha padecido Blue Demon Jr: Entre las victorias más destacadas de Blue Demon Jr fue a los 42 años de edad al derrotar al estadounidense Adam Pierce para convertirse en el campeón mundial de peso completo más longevo de la NWA. En México, sus épicos triunfos contra 'El hijo del Santo', 'Dr Wagner jr' y otros héroes de la lucha libre, serán recordados por siempre y la afición tendrá un años más para disfrutar de Blue Demon Jr antes de colgar la máscara para colocarse la bata de doctor y ayudar a compañeros que hayan caído en las garras del demonio de las lesiones. La gira de Blue Demon Jr. para despedirse comenzará en Irapuato y León, luego se traslada a Monterrey, Ciudad de México, Guadalajara y terminará en Tijuana, ya que fue en esta ciudad fronteriza donde comenzó su carrera profesional. Las carteleras contarán con la participación de Octagón, L.A. Park, Canek Jr, Dr Wagner y Cibernético así como la persona que continuará su legado, su sobrino quien será Blue Demon III.

articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: WBO champion Chantelle Cameron targets 'best performance of career' against Mikaela Mayer
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron vs Mikaela Mayer will headline MVPW-06 at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham; WBO, WBA and WBC super welterweight titles on the line in UK vs USA main event; watch MVPW-06: UK vs USA live on Sky Sports on Saturday August 29
articles.body:
British world champion Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham on August 29 - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

Cameron maintains Mayer - who holds the WBC and WBA belts - is not "special" enough to threaten her chances of victory.

"I really do believe this is going to be a great performance by me - I think it's going to be my best performance of my career, I really do," Cameron told Sky Sports.

"I feel like everything's gone well and there's no reason for it to fall apart on fight night. When I'm like this, and I've put the work in and my mindset is where I want it to be, nobody's beating me.

"I know that all I have to do is do what I've been doing in the gym. I've done everything.

"I'm heading into fight week in such a good place - confident and knowing that it's going to take someone really good and special to beat me, and I just don't think that's Mikaela.

"When I'm thinking like that and acting that out in the gym and everything else, I just know that I'm not going to be denied the victory."

'This would be my second biggest career achievement'

Cameron - WBO champion - is the only fighter to beat Irish boxing legend Katie Taylor, but is aware a victory against Mayer would rank high on her list of achievements.

"It's going to be obviously massive. I am the only one to beat Katie Taylor, so that is going to be hard to top!

"I don't think that's ever going to be topped because Katie Taylor is obviously a phenomenal fighter and nobody has beat her. Everyone's tried, but nobody has actually got that win against her, whereas I have.

"Mikaela's a great fighter, pound for pound, one of the best. This will be my second highest achievement.

"I'm going to say it's a 52 per cent versus 48 per cent kind of job - this is a great fight!

"This is not going to be an easy fight by all means. It's going to be a tough, tough fight, but I know what I'm capable of and I'm excited to execute it.

"When I have this little bite in me and when I have this little like kick in me, I just think nobody's staying with me!"

articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: Caroline Dubois eyes Alycia Baumgardner and Elif Nur Turhan fights after Ameila Moore clash
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois will take on Amelia Moore in Birmingham on August 29; the event will be headlined by Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron, who will compete for the unified welterweight world championship; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Dubois will seek to maintain her unbeaten record when she defends her WBC and WBO straps against Moore at MVPW-06 at the bp pulse LIVE, live on Sky Sports, in their bout on the undercard of Chantelle Cameron's clash with Mikaela Mayer.

While the British boxer asserts she is chomping at the bit for her upcoming fight, she is not shy about using her platform to share her loftier ambitions to unify the world lightweight division.

"To be honest, I always think about what's next," Dubois told Sky Sports .

"Not to be distracted about what is in front of me, but I believe in setting goals. I believe in setting little goals, big goals, massive goals and having timelines.

"For me, the biggest timeline has to be becoming undisputed. We have two more champions in the weight division, [Stephanie] Han and [Elif Nur] Turhan. Whichever one makes the most sense, whichever one is more feasible and accessible for the next fight, we have to go after that.

"It's not about announcing myself - I've already been announced - but cementing myself as the world champion and proving to the world why I'm the world champion, why I'm the only unified world champion.

"It's about sending a message to the rest of the 135ers [in Dubois' weight division] that the queen is in town and this is what's up - I'm coming for the belts!"

Dubois and Moore shared an icy stare down as the pair faced off on Tuesday, the latter insisting she is unshakeable while her champion London rival suggested she has seen nothing in Moore that could trouble her.

"These are my belts, I've worked very hard for them and Amelia Moore isn't going to do anything to take them from me," said Dubois.

"She was around for three Olympic cycles and I qualified first time. I've seen her coming up in the amateurs. I remember going to Colorado and doing an international training camp and she was there.

"I knew about her from the amateurs, she turned professional of course, she slipped off the radar and now she's back so we'll see.

"This is my time to shine, there's no pressure, just excitement. I can't wait to go out there and perform and have fun, there's no expectations."

'I want to punch her in the face and get this over with'

Dubois has no problem expressing her desire to achieve her long-term targets, but her focus remains firmly on putting in a dominant performance against Moore in Birmingham.

"I just can't wait to step into the ring, punch her in the face and get this over with," she said.

"We're going to see vintage Caroline Dubois and we're going to see complete domination.

"I'm not going to focus too much on getting the stoppage. I'm just going to focus on going out there and having fun.

"I just know I'm going to go out there and do my thing, which is going to be look very good and look very exciting. Body, head, attacks, aggressive - vintage."

Dubois: Baumgardner is playing it safe by not fighting me

The Brit was thrilled to learn that unified junior lightweight champion Alycia Baumgardner - who previously insisted that Dubois still needs to prove herself before earning a fight against her - was set to be ringside for the fight against Moore.

"I didn't know that. Is that true? I need to see her - this is great," Dubois told Sky Sports .

"I'm going to go to the gym with a smile on my face. I'm very excited - I can't wait! This is going to be great.

"Boxing is about rivalries, it's about clashes. At the end of the day, boxing is about two people believing what they're better than each other and clashing. It's very rare, unfortunately, with female boxing where you have a fighter who's confident enough to say that.

"With myself and Alycia, I think we're the only two girls right now, besides Claressa Shields, who's confident enough to say: 'I believe I'm going to take your head off your shoulders and I believe I'm the best in the division.'"

Dubois, though, did not change her critical stance on Baumgardner, who she called "lost" for not agreeing to fight her , and is still targeting a shot at the American.

"Alycia likes to play it safe. She's been beaten already.

"Once you lose in professional boxing, unfortunately, people can be very cutthroat and forget all you did to get there. She's already experienced that and now she wants to play everything safe.

"She wanted to fight Amanda Serrano. She wanted to fight Katie Taylor. She wanted to fight all these women who are retiring and are at the end of their careers. She did not want to go after the big dogs because she knows how dangerous it can be.

"I just want to fight the best. I have no issues - I believe in myself and I back myself, I just want it.

"For me, all I care about is being involved in the biggest fights, the most exciting fights. I just see Alycia as being such an exciting fight for myself."

Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 - live on Sky Sports - in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Dubois a step closer.

articles.title: Alycia Baumgardner to step up to Caroline Dubois' division and fight Elif Nur Turhan for IBF world title
articles.summary: Alycia Baumgardner will challenge IBF lightweight champion Elif Nur Turhan on November 8 in a bid to become a two-weight world champion; victory would move unified super featherweight champion closer to a blockbuster unification showdown with WBC and WBO champion Caroline Dubois
articles.body:
Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

articles.title: UFC Shanghai: Yan Xiaonan puts title talk aside ahead of Denise Gomes fight
articles.summary: MMA News: Yan Xiaonan has spent more than a year away from the UFC. She returns on Saturday in Shanghai as the No. 4-ranked women's strawweight, taking on No. 1.
articles.body: Yan Xiaonan has spent more than a year away from the UFC. She returns on Saturday in Shanghai as the No. 4-ranked women's strawweight, taking on No. 14 Denise Gomes in the co-main event.There is plenty around the fight for Yan to think about. She is 37, has been out of action since April 2025 and returns after a unanimous-decision loss to Virna Jandiroba. Before that, she had beaten Tabatha Ricci in 2024, following her five-round title fight against Zhang Weili at UFC 300. The division, meanwhile, has moved on in her absence, with Mackenzie Dern now holding the belt.Yan, though, is not interested in looking that far ahead. "I am not going to think about the championship right now. Right now, my priority is the first fight. I am going to pay attention to this fight and try to win this fight," she told the Times of India in an exclusive interaction.Yan keeps the title picture out of focusAnd the thought process extends to what comes after Gomes. Asked who would make sense as her next opponent if she wins, Yan did not name a contender. "I am open-minded. I am just waiting for whoever the next opponent is. I don't really care."It is a straightforward philosophy for a fighter whose position in the division makes Saturday important. Yan remains fourth in the UFC rankings, while Gomes is 14th and enters the fight on a four-fight winning streak.A long layoff, but a more experienced fighterFor Gomes, it is an opportunity to make a significant jump. For Yan, it is a chance to re-establish herself after the longest gap between UFC appearances of her career. She does not see the layoff as having left her the same fighter."I am definitely more experienced and more mature since last year. I have more experience, definitely."Yan points instead to the accumulated work - her skills, her strengths and the people around her."I am totally ready for the fight. Whatever skills I have improved, whatever strengths I have, and even the team - the whole team is from the US - have helped me. I am definitely more experienced, and the whole team has improved as well."Denise Gomes presents a very different testThe opponent, meanwhile, does not appear to have generated much anxiety. Gomes 26, has seven knockout wins and has won four consecutive UFC fights, most recently beating Tecia Pennington by unanimous decision in November.What does Yan see as the biggest threat?"There is no threat at all. I am just going to be myself, use whatever I have trained, and perform my game," she said.That confidence will be tested against a younger opponent who has steadily climbed the strawweight rankings. Gomes is fighting the biggest name of her UFC career, while Yan is fighting to keep herself in the part of the division where another title opportunity remains possible.But even the changing title picture - Dern's reign, Zhang Weili's move towards flyweight and Yan's No. 4 position - is not something she wants occupying her mind this week.Shanghai return brings excitement, not pressureThe setting, however, is different. Shanghai marks Yan's return to the city after nine years. UFC's August 29 event is its return to Shanghai, with Yan and Song Yadong giving the promotion two of China's biggest MMA names on the card. Song headlines against Umar Nurmagomedov, while Yan faces Gomes in the co-main event.There is no sense from Yan that the occasion has become a burden. "After nine years, I am returning to Shanghai for the UFC. There is no pressure at all. It is just more exciting, and I am more excited to fight."She will also have Song, her fellow Chinese UFC fighter and Team Alpha Male teammate, alongside her during fight week."We are from the same team, and it definitely improves my confidence. I am really happy to work together with Song Yadong, and hopefully we can both win our fights."Nine years after her last fight in Shanghai, Yan will walk into the Octagon again in her home country. This time, she says, there is no added pressure - only excitement.Watch UFC Fight Night - Nurmagomedov vs Song on August 29, 2026, from 3:30 PM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD, Sony Sports Ten 3 SD & HD (Hindi), Sony Sports Ten 4 SD (Tamil,Telugu, Kannada) & Sony LIV.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren
articles.summary: Talks are ongoing over a possible November blockbuster clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua; an apparent dispute over the location of the fight led to Fury claiming that the event was in "serious doubt"
articles.body:
Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".

However, Fury's promoter Warren has allayed fears the fight could be called off, and insists The Gypsy King would also have preferred it to take place in the UK.

Warren told Sky Sports News : "I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Al-Alsheikh, he will announce that fairly soon.

"I know there's been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out.

"In the meantime, Tyson [Fury] has flown off to the States, he's in Miami and he's preparing for the fight.

"I think they both want the fight at Wembley, but it's out of their hands now. That's not quite right, actually, they could refuse to fight. We don't get the fight we want to see.

"I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I'm wrong, but I think it will go on in America."

'Nothing unusual' for all-British clash to take place abroad

Warren says the fight taking place outside of the UK would be "nothing unusual" in terms of boxing's history.

"You had two massive American heroes in Muhammad Ali and George Foreman," Warren said. "Two American fighters, all the Americans wanted to see it, Vegas wanted to put the fight on, Madison Square Gardens wanted to see it, and it went off to Zaire.

"Everybody thought: 'What on earth was that all about?' But it became not just an iconic fight and an iconic moment in sport.

"Ali had the 'Thrilla in Manila' with Joe Frazier. Joe Bugner fought Ali in Kuala Lumpur, it's nothing unusual.

"I think it's like all sportsmen, say, for example, David Beckham, he went off and played at the end of his career [abroad], and he did that because of the money.

"And that's why these guys are doing this, they are professional boxers.

"Would I like to see it at Wembley? Would all the fans like to see it at Wembley? Of course they would. But they are in the hands of another broadcaster who wants the fight in America."

articles.title: Asian Games boxing selection twist: Sumit Kundu returns after Ministry intervention, Deepak Punia back in reserve
articles.summary: Boxing News: NEW DELHI: In yet another bizarre twist to Indiaâs Asian Games boxing selection, Sumit Kundu has retained his place in the menâs 70kg squad despite lo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In yet another bizarre twist to Indiaâs Asian Games boxing selection, Sumit Kundu has retained his place in the menâs 70kg squad despite losing a fresh trial to Deepak Punia, who has now been relegated to reserve.The sports ministryâs final Indian contingent list has named Kundu in the 11-member boxing team â six men and five women â effectively overriding the outcome of the Boxing Federation of Indiaâs (BFI) closed-door trials at NIS Patiala on August 17.The development raises an obvious question: if Kundu was always going to remain the first-choice boxer, why was the fresh trial conducted in the first place?The BFI had originally finalised its Glasgow CWG and Aichi-Nagoya Asiad squads following trials at NIS Patiala on May 13-15. The decision to reopen three categories â menâs 70kg and 90kg, and womenâs 65kg â came after recommendations from the high-performance unit, support staff and selection committee.Kundu, who had been originally selected, lost to reserve Punia in the 70kg bout and was replaced. The trial minutes stated that the winner would be Rank 1 for the Asiad, while the loser would remain reserve. However, they also carried a caveat that if the ministry and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) did not accept the revised entries, the boxers who had represented India at the CWG would retain their Asiad berths.That is precisely what has happened. Kapil Pokhariya retained his 90kg place after beating Harsh Choudhary, while Parveen Hooda stayed in the womenâs 65kg category after defeating Saneh.BFI sources said the trials were necessitated to identify Indiaâs best medal prospects after the trio failed to win medals at the CWG. Kundu lost 1-4 to Northern Irelandâs Jon McConnell in the pre-quarters in Glasgow.But the process has left both Kundu and Punia paying the price. Sources said Sumit was around 75-76kg before the trial, making repeated weight cuts particularly demanding. After preparing for the CWG and August 17 trial, he must again cut weight for the Asiad, leaving his body completely drained.It has been learnt that the boxing contingent is scheduled to leave India on September 4 for a pre-Games training camp in Japan before travelling directly to the Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Makhachev habla de su futuro en la UFC: "Me esperan al menos tres combates más"
articles.standfirst: El peleador daguestaní quiere seguir defendiendo su cinturón de peso wélter hasta conseguir 20 victorias consecutivas en la compañía
articles.summary: El peleador daguestaní quiere seguir defendiendo su cinturón de peso wélter hasta conseguir 20 victorias consecutivas en la compañía
articles.body: El pasado 15 de agosto Islam Makhachev agrandó aún más su legado tras imponerse por decisión unánime a Ian Garry y defender por primera vez el cinturón de peso wélter. Tras batir el récord histórico de defensas en peso ligero y convertirse en doble campeón subiendo a 170 libras, el número uno del ránking libra por libra volvió a brillar para superar a Anderson Silva y quedarse líder en solitario como el peleador con más victorias consecutivas en la UFC -17-, aunque tiene pensado llegar a las 20. El peleador daguestaní sabe que el peso wélter es la categoría más competitiva de la UFC en la actualidad, por lo que quiere medirse a los nombres más importantes para demostrar que sigue vigente a sus 34 años y todavía tiene gasolina en el tanque. Es cierto que aún no ha conseguido finalizar a ningún oponente tras subir de división, pero su grappling de élite le ha bastado para dominar a dos oponentes duros como Ian Garry y Jack Della Maddalena. Tras su llegada a Daguestán, el mejor amigo de Khabib Nurmagomedov fue entrevistado por 'Ushatayka', afirmando que "no sé qué otros récords podré batir, pero ahora mismo en mi categoría hay algunos aspirantes al título muy fuertes. De cara al futuro, creo que me esperan al menos tres combates más". Todo hace indicar que su siguiente rival será Carlos Prates, que parece haber tomado la delantera a Michael Morales. El peleador brasileño de los 'Fighting Nerds' es el striker más temible de la división, aunque muchos dicen que Islam le prefiere porque será más fácil de derribar que Morales, Rakhmonov u otro tipo de peleador con mejor defensa de lucha que 'The Nightmare'. Makhachev ya ha afirmado que quiere volver antes del Ramadán del año que viene para no esperar tanto tiempo hasta su siguiente defensa, y ha sido Prates el que le ha retado para verse las caras en el Madison Square Garden de Nueva York en el UFC 334 de noviembre. Sin embargo, tres meses parecen muy pocos para que le dé tiempo al daguestaní a realizar un nuevo campamento y recuperarse de sus heridas en la cara. En ese mismo escenario fue donde hace un año Makhachev se convirtió en doble campeón tras dominar a Jack Della Maddalena, y donde Prates demostró que puede noquear a cualquiera tras ser el primero que lo hacía ante todo un ex campeón como Leon Edwards. De momento habrá que esperar, pero sus caminos parecen destinados a encontrarse más pronto que tarde, ya que ambos han dado luz verde para que suceda.

articles.title: Boxing: Moses Itauma says Filip Hrgovic's taunts are winding him up before world title fight
articles.summary: Moses Itauma says Filip Hrgovic's comments are starting to "wind him up" before their fight on Saturday.
articles.body:
Moses Itauma says Filip Hrgovic's comments are starting to "wind him up" before their IBF heavyweight world title fight on Saturday.

A victory at the O2 Arena would mean 21-year-old Itauma becomes the second youngest heavyweight world champion in history, behind only Mike Tyson.

The British fighter is the favouite going into the contest, but Hrgovic has been trying to taunt his rival by calling him a "kid" and "inexperienced".

"I tell myself there's nothing that this Hrgovic guy can do to get in my head but he's starting to wind me up," Itauma said.

"In an interview earlier, apparently he said I wake up and I just hug trees. He's really starting to annoy me.

"In my mind if somebody's trying to get one up on you, or trying to get in your head, it's because they're not confident in themselves. Obviously Hrgovic is a talker."

Croatia's Hrgovic, 13 years Itauma's senior, has suggested that victory for his opponent could have a negative affect on Itauma's future and that losing the fight would "save his soul".

"He's already in the clouds. He's already delusional," Hrgovic said.

"It can ruin your soul, it can make you lose yourself and we've seen a lot of superstars and famous people who have lost themselves.

"They're just lost in that crazy world of fame and money. He's not ready for that. I think, for him, it would be best to lose this fight, to save his soul.

"Because what does it mean to achieve everything if you lose your soul and you lose yourself?"

Itauma has had a fast rise to the peak of the boxing mountain, making his professional debut less than four years ago and having 14 fights in that time, knocking his opponent out in all but two of them.

"I wouldn't say he has a point but if I win this fight it might not be good for my soul," Itauma conceded.

"That's not the reason why I'm just gonna go in there and not win â for the sake of my soul. That's not a good idea."

articles.title: Islam Makhachev Reveals How Many UFC Fights He Has Left
articles.summary: UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev revealed how many fights he has left in his UFC career before he retires from MMA.At age 34, Makhachev is still in...
articles.body:
UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev revealed how many fights he has left in his UFC career before he retires from MMA.

At age 34, Makhachev is still in the prime of his athletic career. He is 29-1 in MMA, including an 18-1 record in the UFC, and recently set the longest win streak in promotional history with 17 straight victories.

He is a two-division UFC champion, and he is the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in the world right now. Having accomplished so much, there has been some chatter that Makhachev could walk away on top of his game, just like his friend and teammate Khabib Nurmagomedov did.

But Makhachev says he's not done just yet.

Islam Makhachev Says He Has 3 UFC Fights Left

Speaking to reporters in Dagestan after defeating Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 , Makhachev revealed how many fights he has left in his UFC career, saying he has at least three more fights left in him against really tough opponents.

"Well, I wouldn't call (the win streak record) unbreakable by any means. There are fighters out there, not exactly breathing down my neck, but there are those that already have 10 wins (in a row). I don't know, maybe the title fights record? Though the record for title fights is quite large. I fought 10 bouts before getting the title, while the record holder fought for the title in his third or fourth fight. So I don't know what records will come next, but in my weight class I have some very good title contenders. I think I have at least three more spectacular and very tough fights for me," Makhachev said (via MMAFighting.com ).

After beating Makhachev at UFC 330, the Russian will likely fight Carlos Prates for his next fight, either later this year or early next year. Although the UFC hasn't announced anything yet, the smart money is on Prates getting the title shot.

Michael Morales is another top contender vying for the UFC welterweight title, and you can't completely forget about Shavkat Rakhmonov, the former No. 1 contender who hasn't fought in nearly two years due to injuries.

articles.title: Charles Oliveira Calls for UFC Rematch With Justin Gaethje
articles.summary: UFC BMF champion Charles Oliveira called for a rematch against Justin Gaethje, with both the BMF and lightweight titles on the line. Oliveira defeated Gaethj...
articles.body:
UFC BMF champion Charles Oliveira called for a rematch against Justin Gaethje, with both the BMF and lightweight titles on the line.

Oliveira defeated Gaethje in the main event of UFC 274 in May 2022 in a fight in which Oliveira, who was the UFC lightweight champion at the time, missed weight on the scale.

During the fight, Gaethje knocked the Brazilian down early on in the bout, but Oliveira regained his composure and was able to submit Gaethje soon thereafter after scoring. knockdown of his own.

Now, four years later, Oliveira is calling for the two to fight again, this time with Gaethje as the champion and Oliveira chasing his belt.

Charles Oliveira Wants Rematch With Justin Gaethje

Speaking to Brazilian MMA reporter Olhar da Luta, Oliveira made it clear that he wants Gaethje next with both the BMF and UFC lightweight titles on the line.

"With all due respect, I'm not looking backward. I'm looking forward. I want to fight for the title. That's what I'm focused on. The UFC likes a story… I was robbed (in our first fight). They wanted to distract me so I would go in there, have an (expletive) fight, and they could crown him champion. He felt my hands, I dropped him and then I submitted him. There's a story there. And now he's the champion. I have no problem with that. The rematch doesn't need to be in Brazil. Just like I went to his home turf before, it can be in his backyard, it can be in Las Vegas, on the street corner, in Japan, anywhere in the world. I just need one phone call telling me the date and time. So if the UFC wants a story, what bigger story is there than that?" Oliveira said.

While Oliveira vs. Gaethje is a fine rematch, it's hard to say that Oliveira deserves the title shot more than the winner of the UFC 331 co-main event between Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy, a fight that seems like a No. 1 contender bout.

Oliveira was actually slated to fight Tsarukyan originally on this card, but after his long-time teammate Allan Nascimento passed away, Oliveira was forced to withdraw from the bout, which is understandable.

We'll see what the UFC ultimately decides to do, but there is no doubt a rematch between Oliveira and Gaethje would be fun for the fans to watch.

Heavyweight Guilherme Uriel earned an offer from the fight promotion for his 50-second submission win over Mario Piazzon in the co-featured contest.

Welterweight Sean Clancy Jr. secured a place on the UFC roster with his second-round TKO win over Gary Balletto Jr. He put an end to the fight with a series of brutal elbows.

Welterweight Ronald Humphrey was offered a UFC contract after his first-round submission win over Alexis Miranda. He forced a bloodied Miranda to tap out to a rear-naked choke.

Middleweight Nick Galanti only needed 35 seconds to finish Carlos Petruzzella via knockout to kick off the night of fights. After dropping Petruzzella with a right hand, Galanti went in for the kill with a series of unanswered punches.

articles.title: The âIndian Rhinoâ Chungreng Koren finds his way back with a UFC contract within reach
articles.summary: MMA News: Chungreng Koren is lighter now. He is also more prepared.That may sound like a simple observation ahead of his Road to UFC Season 5 bantamweight semif.
articles.body: Chungreng Koren is lighter now. He is also more prepared.That may sound like a simple observation ahead of his Road to UFC Season 5 bantamweight semifinal against Japanâs Ryo Tajima in Shanghai on August 28. For Koren, though, the difference between this camp and the one that preceded his quarterfinal is significant.When he arrived in Macau for the opening round in May, Koren had accepted the fight at short notice after initially being named a backup.He missed weight before facing Japanâs previously unbeaten Ryuho Miyaguchi. Still, inside the cage he delivered one of the more impressive performances of the opening round, dropping Miyaguchi with a left hand before finishing him with a rear-naked choke at 4:00 of the second round.This time, Koren says, the preparation has been different.âIt was very different. In the last bout, I just did sauna and tried to lose weight. I didn't want to miss the opportunity, so I went for it,â Koren told TimesofIndia.com ahead of the semifinal bout.âThis time, I was at home for three months. I rested for 10 days. After that, I went for training.âA different camp, a different KorenThe weight issue is something Koren is not avoiding. It was an unwanted footnote to an otherwise important night. But Koren admits that the bigger problem was what happened after his previous defeat.In August 2025, he lost his Matrix Fight Night bantamweight title to Nepalâs Rabindra Dhant. The defeat came after Koren had already seen an earlier Road to UFC opportunity disappear because of contractual obligations. The combination left him struggling with his mental health and, eventually, his discipline.âLast time, [when] I lost; after that, I got depressed. I was thinking that I was going to go to the UFC, but I lost. I lost my mind,â he said.âI used to eat healthy food. I used to do regular training. [After that] I didn't go out of my house. I used to eat whatever I wanted. Because of this, my mental and physical condition went down.âThe correction, for Koren, had to begin with the basics.âIf we want to fight, we have to be disciplined. But I lost my discipline. That's why I could not lose weight. Now, I want to eat healthy food. I want to maintain my body. I want to recoverâ.The numbers tell part of that change. Koren says he came into the previous fight around 71 kg and is now down to around 66-67 kg.There has been work on his game too. After the Dhant loss, Koren travelled to Dagestan, where he trained with wrestlers, strikers and UFC fighters. He had previously described that period as a reset, saying it helped him move away from relying primarily on toughness and pressure and towards greater attention to technique, timing and discipline.Ahead of Tajima, he has also spent time training in Phuket.âI have recently trained in Phuket. I have very good partners there. UFC fighters trained with me and [we] fought together. So, I am ready to give a good performance this time,â Koren said.The improvement he feels most strongly is in his striking. âI have improved my striking,â he said when asked what had changed most since the Dhant defeat.That improvement was visible against Miyaguchi. The Japanese fighter began finding his range early in the second round, landing straight right hands. Koren responded with the left hand that dropped him, followed the opening with ground strikes and eventually moved to the back for the submission.Ryo Tajima presents a different testTajima, though, offers a different problem. He is 11-3 and comes into the semifinal after beating Chinaâs Ti Haitao by split decision in May. Koren sees the Japanese fighter as a more experienced opponent with physical advantages.âAny fighter at this level has to be good, and he has more experience than me. He has a better reach than me. He would put more pressure on me. That's why I study him.âKoren's answer to that reach is straightforward. âI think my biggest advantage against him will be my takedown. He has a long reach. So, I think my biggest advantage against him will be my takedown.âThat may be one of the clearest indications of how Koren expects the fight to develop. Tajima has already shown he can handle a three-round fight and blend wrestling with striking. Koren, meanwhile, is coming off a performance in which he showed he can hurt an opponent on the feet before taking the fight to the ground.There is little interest, though, in looking beyond August 28. Koren is now one win away from the Road to UFC final. A victory would leave him one fight from the UFC contract he has pursued for years.But ask him about that contract and his answer is immediate.âOnly one thing at this time.âWhich is?âTajima.âThe Rabindra Dhant rematch can waitThe other semifinal has its own significance for Koren. Dhant is on the opposite side of the bracket, facing unbeaten New Zealander Kasib Murdoch.A Koren-Dhant rematch therefore remains possible. The first meeting ended with Dhant taking Koren's MFN title. This time, the stakes would be considerably higher.Koren knows that, but does not want to get ahead of himself.âWe have to win this fight first. Both the fighters are good. Rabindranath Dant is good. Whatever happens, I have to win this fight first.âStill, Koren sees the possibility of a rematch differently this time. Their first fight had generated significant interest around his profile, with Koren saying it drew more than 50,000 views on his account. If they meet again with a UFC contract at stake, he believes the interest would be even greater.âLast time, we fought in MFN. I had 50K-plus views on my account. And we had good hype. And if I fight Dant, it will generate good hype.âFor Koren, that makes a potential rematch more than just an opportunity to settle an old score.âIt's a good opportunity, and we will have good history as well. But we will see.âThe pressure of fighting for IndiaWhile the focus for Koren is Tajima, that is partly tactical. It is also about the pressure Koren now feels. Before the tournament began, he spoke about carrying his mother, wife, child, people and country with him. In Shanghai, that responsibility sounds even heavier.âThis is very special. We are fighting not just for ourselves. Not for our family. I am fighting for my country.ââAt the same time, there are a lot of risks. If I lose, there will be two or three people to say good things about me. But there will be 100 people to troll me.âIt is a different way of describing what is at stake. The UFC contract is the obvious prize. He also sees the opportunity as part of a larger problem in Indian MMA: there are fighters, he believes, but not enough regular opportunities for them to develop professionally.âIf we want to grow even more, we have to invest in MMA, we have to participate in tournaments, and then only we can find good fighters,â he said.âIn India, MFN is number one. Then there are Ronin FC, Aturto and we have five or six more. But we don't do it [tournaments] regularly.âWhat Indian MMA needs nextHis argument is simple: more competition would create more fighters.âIn other countries, they have regular tournaments, So if we can invest in 20-25 tournaments for professional fighters; very soon, in two or three years, we will find good fighters.âKoren has already become part of that search for visibility. His first Road to UFC run ended before it started. His second arrived unexpectedly. He then missed weight, stepped into the cage against an unbeaten opponent and won by submission.Now there is no short-notice excuse, no backup status and no need to wonder whether he belongs in the tournament.And Koren's message to the young fighters watching is the same one he has repeated through the setbacks.âFirst of all, you don't have to give up.âHe pauses, then repeats it.âYou don't have to give up.âBut he also offers a warning that comes from his own experience.âAnd this is a very rigorous game. And you have to think 10 times before taking this step. And if you want to move forward, you have to sacrifice first.ââYou have to dedicate yourself. If you sacrifice first, dedication will come. First, you have to sacrifice. You have to move forward. That's all I have to say.âOn August 28, Koren gets another opportunity to move forward. This time, he has had the camp. He has worked on the striking. He says his body is ready. And, at least for now, there is only one name occupying his mind. Tajima.Watch ROAD TO UFC Season 5 SFs (Koren vs Ryo Tajima) on August 28, 2026, from 2:30 PM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD, Sony Sports Ten 3 SD & HD (Hindi), Sony Sports Ten 4 SD (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada) & Sony LIV.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron: Five years from influencers to queens of women's boxing for upstart promoters
articles.summary: On Saturday, Most Valuable Promotions celebrates its fifth anniversary. One of the feistiest upstarts in modern boxing has given a new platform to the world's best female fighters.
articles.body:
On 29 August 29 one of the feistiest upstarts in modern boxing will celebrate a fifth anniversary.

On the same date in 2021, Most Valuable Promotions' headline bout for its inaugural show in Cleveland, Ohio, featured co-founder and online influencer Jake Paul taking on MMA fighter Tyron Woodley in the boxing ring.

MVP's second event, just under four months later in Tampa, Florida, was a Paul-Woodley rematch.

For a long time, MVP's most notable event featured Paul fighting Mike Tyson.

It came at a time when Tyson was so far over the hill that the hill could not be seen in the rearview mirror.

MVP's reputation developed as it put together cards with names and output that were anathema to boxing purists.

The five-year anniversary card, however, shows a side of MVP which has emerged alongside what some would consider its gaudiness.

And perhaps what takes place this weekend offers a better indication of the promotion's future than the fights that have gone before.

The main card features five women's bouts, headlined by Mikaela Mayer taking on Chantelle Cameron to unify the WBA, WBC and WBO light-middleweight belts.

The primary support showcases Caroline Dubois defending her WBC and WBO lightweight titles against Amelia Moore.

MVP, for years dismissed by critics as a snot-nosed upstart of a promotion, is now a major player and the primary UK promoter of women's boxing.

"Respect is the biggest change. I've seen and felt it," Dubois told BBC Sport.

"I remember if you said you're a female boxer, people would look at you like 'ah' â but now people are like 'OK, let's see you fight' â it's not a joke, a gimmick, a side caricature. It's part of the real deal."

Fellow Briton Cameron left promoter Queensberry for MVP last year.

Her WBC interim title fight against Patricia Berghult in November 2024 was a co-main event at Birmingham's BP Pulse Arena.

Eight months later, Cameron fought Jessica Camara at New York's iconic Madison Square Garden on her MVP debut.

She returns to the BP Pulse on Saturday, this time a headline fight for her biggest bout since a 2023 double-header against Katie Taylor.

"MVP are taking over women's boxing," Cameron told BBC Sport. "They've been amazing. Everything they've said they'll do, they've done.

"They got me my world title shot. They got me my Mayer fight. It's all been so quick â it's just my third fight with them."

Before her spell with Queensberry, Cameron had been on Matchroom's books. She beat Taylor, before the Irish superstar avenged the defeat second time around.

"The Katie Taylor fights will always go down in history," she said. "But it dipped. I lost momentum. Went on the shelf. I couldn't get the names, couldn't get the fights, nobody wanted to fight me. I wanted the fights, but they just weren't happening."

Dubois, Cameron, Mayer and Terri Harper are among the top women's boxing talent signed to MVP.

Serrano, Alycia Baumgardner and former undisputed super-bantamweight champion Ellie Scotney are also on board.

So why is MVP the go-to promoter for such female boxing talent?

Dubois has developed a brash new persona since working with MVP - calling out Harper before her previous bout, while some verbal sparring led to a feisty face-off.

Tacky? Some might think so. But it saw Dubois move from fighting at the tiny Park Community Arena in Sheffield to Miami and London's Olympia.

"They've helped me get to that next level," Dubois says. "I want to be involved in the best, the biggest and the most important fights.

"Jake [Paul] brings the social influencer dynamic. He gave me tips and pointers and how I should build fights.

"We're entertainers. It's always good to get that insight from someone who is technically outside of the sport. He has that fresh mindset. MVP have that on lock."

While Dubois defends her titles on Saturday, Harper, who lost their April bout on points, begins her rebuild earlier on the card against Miranda Reyes.

Harper considered retirement after losing to Sandy Ryan in 2024, but she had no such thoughts after defeat by Dubois.

"It's my last roll of the dice to see how far I can push to become a four-weight world champion," Harper told BBC Sport.

"MVP have delivered the fights and a greater audience."

MVP looks to balance its serious stance on women's boxing with its influencer roots - August plans featured an 'MVP x Tiktok Live' event, starring Serrano.

The arena events and headline acts have to stay if MVP is to maintain momentum in women's sport.

"I remember my first amateur fight in Camden, or walking into the gym when I was nine years old," Dubois says.

"Now I'm fighting there and I'm talking about headlining and talking about fighting on Netflix."

If there is one thing an organisation led by Paul can provide, it is talk and spectacle.

For Cameron and Mayer, MVP has the chance to make a real difference in women's boxing.

"I'm an advocate for three-minute rounds," says Cameron. "We've got a long way to go, but if more women started doing what the men do, we can start saying they give us the opportunity for equality for women's boxing."

Fighters like Cameron and Mayer have memories that go back beyond the dawn of MVP. They know how their sport has struggled, and know the work still needed.

"In order for a sport to develop, they need to compete and women are a step behind because we weren't allowed to even compete in the Olympics until 2012," says Mayer.

"It's not going to happen overnight, but this is what we needed to take women's boxing to the next step."
